# civicBoard Minimal Requirements (Business-Focused)

## Vision and Scope
A simple discussion board focused on economic and political topics that supports article posts with image and file attachments. Emphasis is on minimal features, civility, and predictable behavior. Complexity is intentionally avoided to keep usage and implementation straightforward.

Goals
- Enable registered members to publish posts (articles) with optional attachments to support evidence-based discussion.
- Enable readers to comment on posts.
- Allow visitors to browse published content without signing in (configurable), while requiring authentication for writing and reporting.
- Provide minimal reporting and administrative moderation to keep discourse safe and on-topic.

Out of Scope (MVP)
- Rich text formatting beyond plain text and line breaks
- Threaded/nested comments
- Direct messaging or real-time chat
- Advanced search and filters; tags or categories
- Reactions/likes, bookmarks, or follows
- Complex notification systems

## Actors
- Guest: Unauthenticated visitor who can browse published content when public read is enabled.
- User: Authenticated member who can create and manage own posts and comments and report content.
- Admin: Administrator who can moderate content and manage reports; can hide or delete any content.

## Core Capabilities (Business)
- Posts: Title + body with optional image/file attachments; public when published.
- Comments: Flat, text-only comments under a post.
- Attachments: Images and files associated to posts; governed by size/type/count limits; follow parent visibility.
- Browsing: Read-optimized lists ordered by recency with simple pagination.
- Reporting and Moderation: Minimal report flow and admin actions (hide/delete) to keep the board safe.

## Functional Requirements (EARS)

### Posts
- THE civicBoard SHALL allow authenticated users to create posts with a title and body.
- THE civicBoard SHALL require title length between 1 and 120 characters and body length between 1 and 20,000 characters.
- THE civicBoard SHALL publish valid posts immediately and display them in the timeline ordered by newest first.
- WHEN an author edits own post within 30 minutes of publish and inputs meet limits, THE civicBoard SHALL save the update and record an updated timestamp.
- IF an author edits own post after 30 minutes, THEN THE civicBoard SHALL deny the edit and explain that the edit window expired.
- WHEN an author deletes own post, THE civicBoard SHALL remove it from public listings immediately and mark it Deleted.
- WHEN an admin hides a post, THE civicBoard SHALL remove it from public visibility and mark it Hidden until a decision is made.
- WHILE a post is Hidden, THE civicBoard SHALL prevent new comments by non-admin users on that post.
- THE civicBoard SHALL list posts in pages of 20 items ordered newest-first.

### Comments
- THE civicBoard SHALL allow authenticated users to create comments on published posts using plain text.
- THE civicBoard SHALL require comment body length between 1 and 5,000 characters.
- WHEN an author edits own comment within 15 minutes, THE civicBoard SHALL save the update and record an updated timestamp.
- IF an author edits own comment after 15 minutes, THEN THE civicBoard SHALL deny the edit and explain that the edit window expired.
- WHEN an author deletes own comment, THE civicBoard SHALL replace the visible content with a placeholder to preserve conversation continuity.
- WHILE a post is Hidden or Deleted, THE civicBoard SHALL block new comments by non-admin users on that post.

### Attachments (Posts Only)
- THE civicBoard SHALL allow image and file attachments on posts only; comments SHALL NOT accept attachments in the minimal release.
- THE civicBoard SHALL allow up to 5 attachments per post.
- THE civicBoard SHALL limit each attachment to a maximum size of 10 MB and the total combined size per post to 25 MB.
- THE civicBoard SHALL allow image types JPEG, PNG, and GIF; and document type PDF for the minimal release.
- IF any attachment exceeds size, count, or type limits, THEN THE civicBoard SHALL reject only the failing attachment(s) and explain the applicable limit.
- WHEN a post is Hidden, THE civicBoard SHALL restrict access to its attachments to admin and the author; WHEN a post is Deleted, THE civicBoard SHALL prevent non-admin access to its attachments.

### Reporting and Moderation
- THE civicBoard SHALL allow authenticated users to report a post or comment and select a reason from a short list with an optional note up to 500 characters.
- WHEN a report is submitted, THE civicBoard SHALL add the item to an admin review queue and record the reporter and reason.
- WHEN an admin decides, THE civicBoard SHALL apply one of: No Action, Hide, or Delete and record the decision with timestamp and admin identity.
- WHEN content is Hidden, THE civicBoard SHALL remove it from public listings and item views while preserving it for admin and author visibility.

### Browsing and Pagination
- THE civicBoard SHALL present a list of published posts ordered by newest-first in pages of 20.
- WHEN opening a post, THE civicBoard SHALL show the title, body, attachments, author display name, publication time, and comments in a consistent order (oldest-first by default).
- IF an item is not available (e.g., removed), THEN THE civicBoard SHALL show a not-available outcome and link back to the list.

## Authentication and Authorization (Business)
- THE civicBoard SHALL require authentication for creating, editing, deleting, or reporting content; reading published content may be allowed to guests when public-read is enabled.
- THE civicBoard SHALL enforce ownership: users may edit or delete only their own posts and comments; admins may moderate any content.
- WHILE an account is suspended, THE civicBoard SHALL deny content creation and management operations and explain the restriction.
- THE civicBoard SHALL represent authenticated sessions in a way that enables role- and ownership-aware authorization decisions without exposing technical details to users.

## Workflows (Conceptual)

Post creation with attachments
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Start: Create Post"] --> B["Enter Title and Body"]
  B --> C{"Add Attachments?"}
  C -->|"Yes"| D["Validate Files(Type/Size/Count)"]
  C -->|"No"| E["Validate Content"]
  D --> E
  E --> F{"All Valid?"}
  F -->|"No"| G["Show Errors and Keep Draft"]
  F -->|"Yes"| H["Publish Post"]
  H --> I["Visible in Timeline"]
```

Report and moderation flow
```mermaid
graph LR
  R1["User Opens Item"] --> R2["Submit Report(Reason+Note)"]
  R2 --> R3["Queue for Admin"]
  R3 --> R4["Admin Reviews"]
  R4 --> R5{"Decision"}
  R5 -->|"No Action"| R6["Keep Visible"]
  R5 -->|"Hide"| R7["Set Hidden State"]
  R5 -->|"Delete"| R8["Set Deleted State"]
```

## Business Rules and Limits
- Post title: 1–120 characters; Post body: 1–20,000 characters; Comments: 1–5,000 characters.
- Post edit window: 30 minutes; Comment edit window: 15 minutes; number of edits is not separately limited in MVP beyond windows.
- Attachments: up to 5 per post; each ≤10 MB; total ≤25 MB per post; types JPEG/PNG/GIF/PDF.
- Rate limits: up to 5 posts per user per 24 hours; up to 50 comments per user per 24 hours; minimum 10 seconds between posts and 5 seconds between comments.
- Reporting: one report per user per item; predefined reasons include Spam, Harassment, Hate Speech, Misinformation, Off-topic, Other.
- Visibility coupling: attachments follow parent post visibility at all times.

EARS enforcement excerpts
- WHEN limits are exceeded, THE civicBoard SHALL prevent submission and specify which limit was violated.
- WHEN content is Hidden, THE civicBoard SHALL prevent non-admin commenting on that content.
- WHEN a post is Deleted, THE civicBoard SHALL prevent non-admin access to its attachments.

## Error and Exception Outcomes
- Validation failure: identify each failed field and rule; preserve entered text and accepted files in the current session.
- Authentication required: deny write/report actions and request sign-in.
- Permission denied: deny modifications by non-owners and explain ownership rule.
- Not available: treat hidden or deleted items as unavailable to non-admin users.
- Rate limited: deny action and indicate earliest retry time based on the relevant window.
- Partial attachment failure: accept valid files and reject invalid ones with reasons; do not publish broken references.

EARS error statements
- WHEN a post body exceeds 20,000 characters, THE civicBoard SHALL reject the submission and state the maximum allowed.
- WHEN a guest attempts to create a comment, THE civicBoard SHALL deny the action and require sign-in.
- IF the target post is Hidden or Deleted, THEN THE civicBoard SHALL deny new comments and state that the post is unavailable.
- WHEN upload includes a sixth file, THE civicBoard SHALL reject the extra file and state the 5-file limit.

## Non-Functional Expectations (Minimal)
- Latency: list timeline p95 ≤ 1,000 ms; open post with first-page comments p95 ≤ 1,200 ms; create post/comment confirmation p95 ≤ 2,000 ms under normal load.
- Availability: monthly availability ≥ 99.5% excluding scheduled maintenance.
- Privacy and safety: collect minimal personal data (e.g., email, display name); never expose email publicly; avoid logging secrets or attachment contents.
- Auditability: record business-level audit events for post/comment create/edit/delete, attachment upload/remove, report submission, and admin moderation actions; restrict audit access to admins.

## Content Lifecycle (Business)
- States: Published, Hidden, Deleted (soft), Deleted (hard).
- Transitions (posts): Published → Hidden (by admin or author), Hidden → Published (by same actor), Published/Hidden → Deleted (soft) (by owner or admin), Deleted (soft) → Deleted (hard) after retention.
- Transitions (comments): Published → Hidden (by author or admin), Hidden → Published (by same actor), Published/Hidden → Deleted (soft), Deleted (soft) → Deleted (hard) after retention.
- Retention: soft-deleted content is purged after 30 days; unlinked uploads are purged after 7 days.
- Attachment coupling: attachments mirror parent state for visibility and deletion timing.

Lifecycle sketch
```mermaid
graph LR
  P1["Published"] -->|"Hide"| P2["Hidden"]
  P2 -->|"Unhide"| P1
  P1 -->|"Delete"| P3["Deleted (soft)"]
  P2 -->|"Delete"| P3
  P3 -->|"Purge After 30d"| P4["Deleted (hard)"]
```

## Success Criteria and Acceptance (Consolidated)
- WHEN a valid post is created with 0–5 allowed attachments (each ≤10 MB, total ≤25 MB), THE civicBoard SHALL publish it and display it in the timeline ordered newest-first within typical response times.
- WHEN a valid comment is created on a published post, THE civicBoard SHALL display it under the post in oldest-first order by default.
- WHEN a report is submitted with a valid reason, THE civicBoard SHALL record it and make it visible to admins for review; WHEN an admin acts, THE civicBoard SHALL apply the chosen state and record an audit entry.
- WHEN limits (length, count, size, rate) are violated, THE civicBoard SHALL reject the action and identify the specific violated rule.

## Glossary
- Author: The creator of a post or comment.
- Published: Visible to all readers (subject to public-read configuration).
- Hidden: Temporarily removed from public view; visible to admins and the author.
- Deleted (soft): Removed from public view with retention for a limited period.
- Deleted (hard): Permanently removed after the retention period.
- Attachment: Image or file linked to a post that follows the post’s visibility.
- Report: A user-submitted signal requesting admin review of potentially inappropriate content.

plainFields.name: actor_session_id

plainFields.name: outcome

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp to permit safe retention before purge.

models.name: civic_board_users

models.name: civic_board_posts
models.description: Discussion board posts (articles) authored by users. Contains the title, body, and lifecycle status with publication and edit timestamps. Each post is created by a {@link civic_board_users} actor. Optionally links to the authoring {@link civic_board_user_sessions} for audit context without risking content deletion when sessions expire (nullable + onDelete:SetNull). Comments ({@link civic_board_comments}) and attachments ({@link civic_board_post_attachments}) reference this entity. Visibility and moderation operate via status (Published/Hidden/Deleted) and administrative records in {@link civic_board_moderation_actions}.

plainFields.description: Post body text. Business limits: 1–20,000 characters, plain text with line breaks allowed.

plainFields.description: Lifecycle status of the post. Expected values: "Published", "Hidden", or "Deleted". Used to control visibility and commenting eligibility.

Lifecycle status governs visibility and moderation (Published/Hidden/Deleted). Comments are listed oldest-first under a post and support cross-post queries by author.

plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for this record (auditable).

models.name: civic_board_reports
models.description: User-submitted moderation requests (reports) across posts or comments. Holds common report metadata such as reason, optional note, and workflow status. Exactly one specialization row must exist in either {@link civic_board_report_of_posts} or {@link civic_board_report_of_comments} to bind the report to its concrete target. Admins review these records and create {@link civic_board_moderation_actions} as resolutions. Reporters may query their own reports via the specialization tables using the reporter identity.

models.description: User single-like reactions on posts. Each row represents at most one reaction per (user, post) pair. The reaction is considered active when not soft-deleted (deleted_at is NULL). ### `civic_board_configurations`

System-wide configuration entries stored as independent key-value
records. Used to toggle features, define thresholds, or set URIs across
the platform. This table is intentionally decoupled from domain content
and identities to avoid dependency cycles. Managed primarily by
administrators through configuration UIs or scripts; referenced by
runtime services to read current settings. No foreign keys are declared
to other domains.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `key`
  > Unique configuration identifier (e.g., "public_read",
  > "attachments.max_count"). Serves as the business key for lookups.
- `value_string`
  > String value for this configuration when applicable. Only one of the
  > typed value columns is expected to be used per row.
- `value_int`
  > Integer value for this configuration when applicable (e.g., numeric
  > limits).
- `value_double`
  > Decimal value for this configuration when applicable (e.g., thresholds or
  > ratios).
- `value_boolean`
  > Boolean value for this configuration when applicable (e.g., feature
  > toggle).
- `value_uri`
  > URI value for this configuration when applicable (e.g., callback URLs,
  > CDN endpoints).
- `description`: Human-readable explanation of the configuration purpose and usage.
- `effective_since`: Optional timestamp indicating when this configuration became effective.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp (UTC).
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp (UTC).
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp for retention and operational safety.

### `civic_board_policies`

System policies governing platform behavior such as public-read,
moderation defaults, and feature switches. Each policy is an
independently managed record with an optional effective window. This
table is maintained by administrators and does not reference domain
content directly. Related changes are recorded in {@link
civic_board_audit_logs}.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `policy_code`
  > Stable policy identifier (e.g., "public_read", "attachments.policy",

- `value_double`

Append-only audit trail capturing security- and compliance-relevant
events across the system. Records the acting entity (user/admin/system),
optional session context, target reference, action name, outcome, and
request metadata. Designed for historical analysis and investigations;
not intended for direct user manipulation. This table provides the
system’s audit history for changes in [civic_board_policies](#civic_board_policies) and

### `civic_board_users`

Registered member accounts for the civicBoard application. Stores
authentication credentials and profile-facing display attributes. Serves
as the primary identity for regular users who author posts and comments.
Related entities include session records {@link
civic_board_user_sessions} and verification/reset flows via {@link
civic_board_email_verification_of_users} and {@link
civic_board_password_reset_token_of_users}.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Login and contact email for the user. Must be unique across all users and
  > used for verification workflows.
- `password_hash`
  > BCrypt or similar password hash for authentication. Never store plain
  > passwords.
- `display_name`
  > Public display name shown on authored content instead of email for
  > privacy.
- `email_verified`
  > Whether the user’s email has been verified. Governs posting/commenting
  > eligibility.
- `suspended`
  > Whether the account is currently suspended and restricted from creating
  > or modifying content.
- `suspended_at`: Timestamp when the account was suspended, if applicable.
- `created_at`: Record creation time (UTC).
- `updated_at`: Last update time (UTC).
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion time (UTC). Null when active.

### `civic_board_user_sessions`

Authenticated session records for [civic_board_users](#civic_board_users). Follows the
exact session table pattern: one actor FK, connection context (ip, href,
referrer), created_at, and optional expired_at. Managed through
authentication flows for audit and authorization context.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `civic_board_user_id`: Belonged user’s [civic_board_users.id](#civic_board_users)
- `ip`: IP address observed when establishing the session.
- `href`: Full URL that initiated the session (connection URL).

board-level policies. Related entities include {@link

civic_board_email_verification_of_admins} and {@link
civic_board_password_reset_token_of_admins}.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Login and contact email for the admin. Must be unique across all admins

### `civic_board_posts`

Discussion board posts (articles) authored by users. Contains the title,
body, and lifecycle status with publication and edit timestamps. Each
post is created by a [civic_board_users](#civic_board_users) actor. Optionally links to
the authoring [civic_board_user_sessions](#civic_board_user_sessions) for audit context without
risking content deletion when sessions expire (nullable +
onDelete:SetNull). Comments ([civic_board_comments](#civic_board_comments)) and
attachments ([civic_board_post_attachments](#civic_board_post_attachments)) reference this entity.
Visibility and moderation operate via status (Published/Hidden/Deleted)
and administrative records in [civic_board_moderation_actions](#civic_board_moderation_actions).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `civic_board_user_id`: Author user's [civic_board_users.id](#civic_board_users).
- `civic_board_user_session_id`
  > Authoring session's [civic_board_user_sessions.id](#civic_board_user_sessions). Nullable and
  > set null on session deletion to preserve content.
- `title`: Post title. Business limits: 1–120 characters, trimmed, non-whitespace.
- `body`
  > Post body text. Business limits: 1–20,000 characters, plain text with
  > line breaks allowed.
- `status`
  > Lifecycle status of the post. Expected values: "Published", "Hidden", or
  > "Deleted". Used to control visibility and commenting eligibility.
- `published_at`
  > Publication timestamp recorded when the post becomes publicly visible
  > (Published).
- `edited_at`
  > Last content edit timestamp within the allowed edit window; null if never
  > edited.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp (auditable).
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for this record (auditable).
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp. Null when active; set when Deleted to support
  > retention/purge policies.

### `civic_board_post_attachments`

File attachments associated with posts. Attachments inherit visibility
rules from their parent [civic_board_posts](#civic_board_posts). Each row stores
immutable file metadata and storage URI. Only posts (not comments) can
have attachments. Uploaded by a user through a session for auditability.
Session link is nullable and set null on deletion to avoid unintended
content loss.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `civic_board_post_id`: Parent post's [civic_board_posts.id](#civic_board_posts).
- `civic_board_user_id`: Uploader user's [civic_board_users.id](#civic_board_users).
- `civic_board_user_session_id`
  > Uploader session's [civic_board_user_sessions.id](#civic_board_user_sessions). Nullable and set
  > null on session deletion to preserve the attachment record.
- `uri`: Storage URI pointing to the attached file object.
- `original_filename`
  > User-facing original filename after sanitization; used for display and
  > duplicate prevention per post.
- `content_type`
  > MIME type detected/accepted (e.g., image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif,
  > application/pdf).
- `byte_size`
  > File size in bytes; used to enforce per-file and per-post total limits in
  > application logic.
- `image_width`
  > Image width in pixels if the attachment is an image; null for non-image
  > types.
- `image_height`
  > Image height in pixels if the attachment is an image; null for non-image
  > types.
- `created_at`: Attachment creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Attachment last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp for retention/purge handling.

### `civic_board_comments`

Plain-text comments on posts. Each comment belongs to a {@link
civic_board_posts} and is authored by a [civic_board_users](#civic_board_users).
Optionally links the [civic_board_user_sessions](#civic_board_user_sessions) for audit context
without risking content deletion (nullable + onDelete:SetNull). Lifecycle
status governs visibility and moderation (Published/Hidden/Deleted).
Comments are listed oldest-first under a post and support cross-post
queries by author.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `civic_board_post_id`: Target post's [civic_board_posts.id](#civic_board_posts).
- `civic_board_user_id`: Author user's [civic_board_users.id](#civic_board_users).
- `civic_board_user_session_id`
  > Authoring session's [civic_board_user_sessions.id](#civic_board_user_sessions). Nullable and
  > set null on session deletion to preserve the comment.
- `body`
  > Comment body text. Business limits: 1–2,000 characters (minimal scope);
  > text-only (no attachments).
- `status`
  > Lifecycle status of the comment. Expected values: "Published", "Hidden",
  > or "Deleted".
- `published_at`: Timestamp when the comment became publicly visible (Published).
- `edited_at`: Last edit timestamp within the 15-minute window; null if never edited.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp (auditable).
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for this record (auditable).
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp for retention/purge policies.

### `civic_board_reports`

User-submitted moderation requests (reports) across posts or comments.
Holds common report metadata such as reason, optional note, and workflow
status. Exactly one specialization row must exist in either {@link
civic_board_report_of_posts} or [civic_board_report_of_comments](#civic_board_report_of_comments) to
bind the report to its concrete target. Admins review these records and
create [civic_board_moderation_actions](#civic_board_moderation_actions) as resolutions. Reporters
may query their own reports via the specialization tables using the
reporter identity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `reason`
  > Reporter-selected categorical reason (e.g., Spam, Harassment, Off-topic,
  > Other). Business validation occurs at application level.
- `note`
  > Optional free-text note from the reporter, up to 500 characters per
  > business rules.
- `status`
  > Workflow state of this report such as "pending" or "resolved" for queue
  > management.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp (UTC) when the report was filed.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp (UTC) for this report metadata.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp (UTC) when the report is removed from
  > public/admin queues but retained for policy retention.

### `civic_board_report_of_posts`

Specialization of [civic_board_reports](#civic_board_reports) that binds a report to a
specific post and captures the reporter identity and session for audit
and constraint enforcement. One-to-one with [civic_board_reports](#civic_board_reports).
Prevents duplicate reports by the same user on the same post via a
composite unique constraint.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `civic_board_report_id`
  > Parent report's [civic_board_reports.id](#civic_board_reports). Enforces 1:1
  > specialization.
- `civic_board_post_id`: Target post's [civic_board_posts.id](#civic_board_posts).
- `civic_board_user_id`: Reporting user's [civic_board_users.id](#civic_board_users).
- `civic_board_user_session_id`: Reporting session's [civic_board_user_sessions.id](#civic_board_user_sessions).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp (UTC) when this specialization was created.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp (UTC) for this specialization.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp (UTC) if this specialization is logically removed.

### `civic_board_report_of_comments`

Specialization of [civic_board_reports](#civic_board_reports) that binds a report to a
specific comment and captures the reporter identity and session for audit
and constraint enforcement. One-to-one with [civic_board_reports](#civic_board_reports).
Prevents duplicate reports by the same user on the same comment via a
composite unique constraint.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `civic_board_report_id`
  > Parent report's [civic_board_reports.id](#civic_board_reports). Enforces 1:1
  > specialization.
- `civic_board_comment_id`: Target comment's [civic_board_comments.id](#civic_board_comments).
- `civic_board_user_id`: Reporting user's [civic_board_users.id](#civic_board_users).
- `civic_board_user_session_id`: Reporting session's [civic_board_user_sessions.id](#civic_board_user_sessions).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp (UTC) when this specialization was created.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp (UTC) for this specialization.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp (UTC) if this specialization is logically removed.

### `civic_board_moderation_actions`

Administrative resolution records for [civic_board_reports](#civic_board_reports).
Captures the acting admin and session with the chosen decision (Hide,
Delete, or No Action) and an optional note. Enforces a single resolution
per report via a unique FK, creating an immutable audit trail separate
from content state changes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `civic_board_report_id`: Resolved report's [civic_board_reports.id](#civic_board_reports). One action per report.
- `civic_board_admin_id`: Acting administrator's [civic_board_admins.id](#civic_board_admins).
- `civic_board_admin_session_id`: Administrator session's [civic_board_admin_sessions.id](#civic_board_admin_sessions).
- `decision`: Resolution outcome string such as "No Action", "Hide", or "Delete".
- `outcome_note`: Optional moderator note providing rationale for the decision.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp (UTC) when the moderation action was recorded.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp (UTC) for this moderation action record.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp (UTC) if the action record is withdrawn
  > administratively.

### `civic_board_post_reactions`

User single-like reactions on posts. Each row represents at most one
reaction per (user, post) pair. The reaction is considered active when
not soft-deleted (deleted_at is NULL). Designed to support toggle
semantics by updating timestamps while preserving auditability.
References [civic_board_users](#civic_board_users) as the reacting actor and {@link
civic_board_posts} as the target content. Hidden or Deleted targets must
block new reactions at the application layer; self-like is prevented by
business rules.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `civic_board_user_id`: Reacting user's [civic_board_users.id](#civic_board_users).
- `civic_board_post_id`: Target post's [civic_board_posts.id](#civic_board_posts).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp when the reaction was first added (Like on).
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp, including toggling operations.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp representing Like off toggle. NULL means the
  > reaction is currently active.

### `civic_board_comment_reactions`

User single-like reactions on comments. Each row represents at most one
reaction per (user, comment) pair. The reaction is active when deleted_at
is NULL, enabling toggle behavior without losing history. References
[civic_board_users](#civic_board_users) as the reacting actor and {@link
civic_board_comments} as the target comment. Hidden or Deleted targets
must block new reactions at the application layer; self-like is prevented
by business rules.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `civic_board_user_id`: Reacting user's [civic_board_users.id](#civic_board_users).
- `civic_board_comment_id`: Target comment's [civic_board_comments.id](#civic_board_comments).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp when the reaction was first added (Like on).
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp, including toggling operations.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp representing Like off toggle. NULL means the
  > reaction is currently active.

### `civic_board_reaction_policies`

Administrative policy controlling whether reactions are enabled and under
what constraints. This table allows feature toggling and guardrails such
as self-like prohibition and per-user rate limits. It is managed
independently by admins and referenced by application logic at runtime.
Does not denormalize any computed counters. Related entities: users
[civic_board_users](#civic_board_users) for ownership context if needed; targets are
[civic_board_posts](#civic_board_posts) and [civic_board_comments](#civic_board_comments).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `code`
  > Human-readable policy code identifier (e.g., "default"). Used to select
  > the active configuration.
- `enabled`: Whether reactions feature is globally enabled.
- `allow_on_posts`: Whether reactions are permitted on posts.
- `allow_on_comments`: Whether reactions are permitted on comments.
- `allow_self_like`
  > Whether self-like is permitted. Should remain false to satisfy product
  > rules.
- `max_reactions_per_user_per_day`
  > Optional cap on the number of reactions a single user may add per
  > calendar day. NULL means unlimited per this policy.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp of this policy row.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp of this policy row.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp for deprecated or replaced policies. NULL means
  > active.

operations.specification: Create a registration endpoint for the member actor based on the civic_board_users table. This operation inserts a new record into civic_board_users using fields email, password_hash (derived from submitted password), display_name, and initializes email_verified to false and suspended to false. It should also create an initial session in civic_board_user_sessions (fields: civic_board_user_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at) and may issue an email verification token by inserting into civic_board_email_verifications (actor_type="user", email, token, expires_at, used=false) plus a specialization row in civic_board_email_verification_of_users linking the token to the new user via civic_board_user_id. Successful registration returns JWTs in an authorized payload while persisting an audit trail via civic_board_audit_logs as appropriate. Prisma tables directly involved: civic_board_users (primary), civic_board_user_sessions, civic_board_email_verifications, civic_board_email_verification_of_users, and optionally civic_board_audit_logs for audit entries.
operations.description:
This operation registers a new member account by creating a record in civic_board_users. It consumes the submitted email to populate civic_board_users.email, stores a cryptographic password hash in civic_board_users.password_hash, and saves the user-facing name in civic_board_users.display_name. New accounts are created with civic_board_users.email_verified set to false and civic_board_users.suspended set to false. Timestamps civic_board_users.created_at and civic_board_users.updated_at are set to the current UTC time.

Upon successful creation, the system records a session entry in civic_board_user_sessions tied with civic_board_user_sessions.civic_board_user_id to the new user. Connection context from the request is captured in civic_board_user_sessions.ip, civic_board_user_sessions.href, and civic_board_user_sessions.referrer with civic_board_user_sessions.created_at set to the current UTC time. The session remains active until civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at is populated by a later logout or session revocation.

If email confirmation is required, an email verification token is produced by inserting a row into civic_board_email_verifications with actor_type set to "user", email mirrored into civic_board_email_verifications.email, a unique civic_board_email_verifications.token, and civic_board_email_verifications.expires_at scheduled according to policy while civic_board_email_verifications.used remains false. The token is linked to the user by creating a specialization row in civic_board_email_verification_of_users referencing civic_board_email_verification_of_users.civic_board_email_verification_id and civic_board_email_verification_of_users.civic_board_user_id.

Security logic enforces uniqueness on civic_board_users.email (per the @@unique constraint) and applies initial eligibility rules using civic_board_users.email_verified and civic_board_users.suspended. Passwords are never persisted in plain text; only civic_board_users.password_hash is stored.

Related operations include POST /auth/user/login for subsequent authentications, POST /auth/user/email/verify/request for re-sending verification tokens, and POST /auth/user/email/verify/confirm for token confirmation. Failures such as duplicate email or invalid input yield clear validation errors while preserving safe behavior.

On success, this endpoint issues an authorized response containing access credentials appropriate for subsequent requests and may optionally record an audit entry in civic_board_audit_logs using fields like actor_type, action, outcome, and created_at to provide compliance visibility.
operations.summary: Register a new member in civic_board_users and return authorized tokens.

requestBody.description: Registration payload containing email, password, and display name.

responseBody.description: Authorized session and token package for the newly registered user.
