operations.specification:
Update a specific post attachment record stored in the civic_board_post_attachments table, identified by its UUID and scoped under its parent post civic_board_posts. This operation enables controlled modification of attachment metadata and/or file pointer (uri) while enforcing business policies for allowed content types, size limits, per-post attachment count, and uniqueness of original_filename per post (@@unique([civic_board_post_id, original_filename])). The path parameters carry the postId (civic_board_posts.id) and the attachmentId (civic_board_post_attachments.id). The provider must validate that the target attachment actually belongs to the indicated post (civic_board_post_attachments.civic_board_post_id = postId) before applying an update. Ownership and time-window rules derive from the post’s lifecycle and the attachment’s uploader fields (civic_board_post_attachments.civic_board_user_id and optional civic_board_user_session_id).

The request body follows ICivicBoardPostAttachment.IUpdate and may include fields such as uri, original_filename, and content_type, as well as any other mutable columns defined in the DTO that map to real columns (e.g., byte_size and image dimensions when the underlying file is replaced). The response returns the fully updated ICivicBoardPostAttachment object. Implementers must ensure changes remain consistent with the civic_board_posts state (status: "Published" | "Hidden" | "Deleted") and business edit windows and must not violate the composite uniqueness on (civic_board_post_id, original_filename).
operations.description:
Modify an existing post attachment while adhering to the schema-level intent documented on civic_board_post_attachments and civic_board_posts. The civic_board_post_attachments table stores immutable file metadata and storage URI with columns such as uri (VarChar up to 80000), original_filename, content_type, byte_size, optional image_width/height, timestamps, and an optional deleted_at used for retention. Its relation to civic_board_posts is a required FK (post) that must be respected; an attachment always belongs to exactly one post. Before applying any update, the service verifies that the path’s {postId} corresponds to the row’s civic_board_post_id and that the path’s {attachmentId} matches the target attachment’s id.

Security and authorization are enforced using actor context from civic_board_users and, when present, civic_board_user_sessions captured on upload. As per business rules, authors may modify attachments of their own posts only within the allowed edit window for posts (civic_board_posts has published_at, edited_at, and status fields). Admins may act at any time per moderation policy. If an attachment has a non-null deleted_at, treat it as removed from active visibility and disallow ordinary updates.

This operation is tightly coupled to the underlying database entities. It updates columns on civic_board_post_attachments that are meant to change when a file pointer or metadata legitimately changes (e.g., uri, original_filename, content_type, byte_size, image_width, image_height) and refreshes updated_at. The unique constraint @@unique([civic_board_post_id, original_filename]) is enforced to prevent duplicate display names per post. Ensure any change remains coherent with the parent post’s status in civic_board_posts (status: "Published" | "Hidden" | "Deleted").

Validation rules include: honoring allowed MIME types (e.g., image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, application/pdf), respecting size limits reflected by byte_size, and ensuring that attachment visibility follows the parent post’s visibility state. Related APIs commonly used together include: deleting an attachment (DELETE /posts/{postId}/attachments/{attachmentId}) and post editing endpoints that govern the author’s edit window. On errors, return business-appropriate outcomes for ownership violations, edit-window expiry, hidden/deleted parent states, uniqueness conflicts on original_filename, and attempts to update an attachment that does not belong to the given post.

Remove a specific post attachment row from civic_board_post_attachments identified by {attachmentId} and scoped by its parent post {postId}. The table includes a deleted_at column; therefore, this operation performs a soft deletion by setting deleted_at instead of physically removing the row, supporting retention and purge policies aligned with the business lifecycle. The path parameters are postId (civic_board_posts.id) and attachmentId (civic_board_post_attachments.id). The provider must verify that the attachment belongs to the specified post before proceeding.

This operation supports author-driven removal within the allowed post edit window and administrative moderation at any time. Attachment visibility always follows the parent civic_board_posts record (status: "Published" | "Hidden" | "Deleted"). When deleted, the attachment should immediately disappear from public listings and reads, while remaining retained for administrative purposes until purge jobs finalize permanent removal according to policy.
operations.description:
Permanently remove the attachment from active visibility by marking the civic_board_post_attachments record with a non-null deleted_at timestamp. According to the schema comments, attachments inherit visibility from the parent post and store immutable file metadata such as uri, original_filename, content_type, and byte_size. The presence of deleted_at indicates the record is no longer active. Before removal, confirm that the given {postId} matches the record’s civic_board_post_id and that {attachmentId} matches the target attachment’s id, preventing cross-post access.

Security and permissions follow the business rules: the author may remove attachments tied to their own post within the edit window described by civic_board_posts timestamps; admins may remove attachments at any time as part of moderation. Attempts to remove attachments on posts in states that disallow user actions (e.g., Hidden or Deleted for non-admins) must be denied. The operation writes only the deleted_at (and updated_at) columns in civic_board_post_attachments; it does not alter the parent civic_board_posts row beyond indirect visibility effects.

Error handling includes: not-available outcomes when the attachment is already deleted; ownership or session checks failing; parent-post mismatch between IDs; or business policy rejections (e.g., post state disallowing user actions). Related operations: updating an attachment (PUT /posts/{postId}/attachments/{attachmentId}) and post-level edit endpoints that determine whether the attachment may be modified by the author at this time.

This operation writes into the Moderation domain by creating one main report row in civic_board_reports and one specialization row in civic_board_report_of_posts that binds the report to the target post and the reporting user/session. The reporter identity (civic_board_user_id) and session (civic_board_user_session_id) are taken from the authenticated context, not from the client payload. Duplicate prevention is enforced by the composite uniqueness on civic_board_report_of_posts (civic_board_user_id, civic_board_post_id). The request body carries only the business fields the reporter provides (reason and optional note), while the path parameter provides the post identifier. Upon success, the created specialization record (ICivicBoardReportOfPost) is returned for immediate client display and follow-up navigation to admin review flows (resolved later by civic_board_moderation_actions).
operations.description:
Submit a moderation report for a post by providing a categorical reason and an optional note. The operation persists report metadata in civic_board_reports with fields reason (text), note (optional text up to the product’s business limit), status (string workflow state such as "pending" managed by application logic), and audit timestamps created_at and updated_at. The specialization civic_board_report_of_posts binds the report to the target post via civic_board_post_id and records the reporting user via civic_board_user_id and the originating session via civic_board_user_session_id. The specialization enforces a one-to-one link to the main report through civic_board_report_id.

Security and permissions: only authenticated users may file reports. The reporter is derived from the signed-in user and their current session; clients must not supply user identifiers directly. Rate limits and duplicate prevention apply per policy; duplicates are structurally prevented by civic_board_report_of_posts @@unique([civic_board_user_id, civic_board_post_id]) so the same user cannot report the same post twice.

Database relationships: the created main report row in civic_board_reports can later be resolved by administrators who record decisions (e.g., Hide, Delete, or No Action) in civic_board_moderation_actions with a 1:1 uniqueness on civic_board_report_id. The report’s status string in civic_board_reports is used by queue processing and can be updated as part of the moderation lifecycle.

Validation and behavior: the request must include a supported reason value and may include an optional note. The server validates that the referenced civic_board_posts.id exists and that the authenticated user has permission to report. If the target post is not visible to the reporter or no longer exists, the service responds with a not-available outcome. The table includes a deleted_at timestamp for retention policies; newly created reports will have this column null. Error handling includes duplicate report detection (based on the unique constraint), invalid reason values per business rules, and authorization failures for unauthenticated actors.

Related operations: administrators will use separate moderation endpoints to resolve reports by creating entries in civic_board_moderation_actions. Reporters may later query their own reports through list endpoints filtered by reporter identity (not part of this operation).

The status field in civic_board_reports supports queue management as the report moves through review. The deleted_at column exists for retention policies and remains null for newly created records.

Validation and behavior: the service validates the existence of the referenced civic_board_comments.id and confirms that the reporter is eligible to report. If the comment is not available to the reporter (e.g., removed or not visible), the service responds with a not-available outcome. Input validation checks that reason meets allowed values and that note length is within the allowed business limit. Error handling includes duplicate detection from the unique constraint, authorization failures for unauthenticated actors, and target-not-found cases.

Related operations: separate administrative endpoints handle resolving reports by writing to civic_board_moderation_actions. Reporters may later view their own report history through listing endpoints, which are outside the scope of this creation operation.

The primary entity carries report metadata such as id (UUID primary key), reason (categorical string), optional note (up to 500 chars per business rules), status (workflow string), created_at/updated_at timestamps, and deleted_at for soft-retention. Retrieve an administrator-facing queue of reports from civic_board_reports. Each report row stores the categorical reason (reason), an optional note (note), a workflow status string (status), and auditable timestamps (created_at, updated_at). The schema comment clarifies that this table is the moderator queue and that exactly one specialization must exist in either civic_board_report_of_posts or civic_board_report_of_comments, which binds the report to its concrete target. Use these relations when the UI needs to show target type or reporter context; however, core filtering in this operation focuses on fields physically present in civic_board_reports.

Access to this listing is restricted to administrators because reports may contain sensitive context and moderation notes. The operation is intended for back-office workflows such as triage, bulk review, and time-based monitoring. While reporters can query their own submissions via specialization-specific endpoints, the generic /reports list is reserved for admin use to prevent information disclosure.

From a data relationship standpoint, civic_board_reports has a 1:1 association with one specialization row and an optional 1:1 association to a civic_board_moderation_actions row recording the final decision (Hide, Delete, or No Action). Duplicate-report prevention is enforced at the specialization layer via composite unique constraints (for example, user + post or user + comment), and not on the civic_board_reports base table itself—providers should rely on those constraints when composing queries.

Validation and business logic include filtering by status (e.g., pending vs resolved), reason categories, and created_at ranges using the actual columns present in the table. Since civic_board_reports includes a deleted_at column, soft-deleted records are excluded by default unless an explicit include-deleted flag is provided by the request body; this matches retention and audit expectations.

This operation is designed to pair with GET /reports/{reportId} for detailed inspection and with moderation action creation endpoints (not defined here) that write to civic_board_moderation_actions. Errors to expect include authorization failures for non-admin actors and empty result sets when filters yield no matches. Pagination is stable and results are ordered by created_at desc by default, with optional sort overrides.

The specialization also holds the reporter’s identity and session for audit. Security and permissions restrict access to administrator actors. Reports can reference sensitive content or reporter notes; therefore, direct access by non-admin users is not allowed on this generic endpoint. Reporter self-service views, when implemented, should be provided through specialization-scoped endpoints that enforce ownership constraints.

Relationship and lifecycle considerations: If a civic_board_moderation_actions record exists for the report, its decision (e.g., Hide, Delete, No Action) reflects the resolution. The civic_board_reports table has deleted_at for soft retention; a report with deleted_at populated may still be retrievable by admins for audit, depending on business rules.

Validation and error handling include UUID format validation for reportId, not-found outcomes when the record is absent or excluded by policy, and authorization denials for non-admin actors. operations.description:
Fetch the moderation resolution associated with a given report. The underlying civic_board_moderation_actions model records administrative resolutions for civic_board_reports, capturing the acting administrator and session identifiers, the decision string, and an optional outcome note. According to the schema comments, this record is the immutable audit trail for how a report was resolved and is strictly one-to-one with its report through a unique foreign key.

Security and permissions: Only administrators should access this endpoint because the action contains moderation decisions and administrative context. The civic_board_admins and civic_board_admin_sessions relations on the action record provide the administrative provenance for auditing. Non-admin actors should not be able to read these records directly.

Database relationship context: The civic_board_moderation_actions row is associated to a parent civic_board_reports entry via civic_board_report_id, and the civic_board_reports entry itself is specialized to either a post or a comment via civic_board_report_of_posts or civic_board_report_of_comments. This endpoint does not require the caller to know which specialization is used; it resolves purely by the report’s UUID.

Validation and expected behavior: If no moderation action exists for the specified reportId (because the report is still pending or has not been decided), the implementation should respond with a not-found outcome for this resource path. If an action exists, it returns the single action. The status field on civic_board_reports (e.g., "pending" or "resolved") is orthogonal but often correlates to the presence of an action.

Create a single moderation decision record for the given report. Per the schema description, the table enforces one action per report via a unique constraint, ensuring a stable audit record.

Security and permissions: Only administrators may create moderation actions. The implementation must validate that the caller is an admin, is not suspended, and that the report exists. The administrator identity and session should be persisted using the relations to civic_board_admins and civic_board_admin_sessions for auditing.

Database relationships and workflow: A civic_board_reports entry exists for every moderation request submitted by users, and is specialized by either civic_board_report_of_posts or civic_board_report_of_comments to bind the concrete target. Creating a moderation action for a report typically corresponds to transitioning the report’s workflow to a resolved state, while the underlying post or comment visibility is changed by separate business logic according to the chosen decision.

Validation and error handling: If an action already exists for the reportId, this operation must fail to honor the unique-per-report rule on civic_board_moderation_actions. If the reportId does not correspond to an existing report, the implementation must return a not-found outcome. The request body must provide a valid decision string, and outcome_note may be supplied when moderation context needs recording.

Related operations: Use GET /reports/{reportId}/moderationAction to retrieve the action after creation. There is no update endpoint in this minimal scope; corrections require administrative workflows outside of this operation.

Given the path parameter postId (civic_board_posts.id) and the authenticated user context (civic_board_users.id), the service will either create a new reaction row or, if a historical row exists with deleted_at set, restore it by clearing deleted_at and updating timestamps. operations.description:
Create or re-activate a post reaction for the authenticated user. The underlying entity is civic_board_post_reactions, which records the reacting user (civic_board_user_id), the target post (civic_board_post_id), and lifecycle timestamps (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at). Per the schema comments, reactions provide toggle semantics by keeping history and marking the reaction inactive via the deleted_at timestamp rather than removing the row. When this endpoint is called, if no reaction exists for the (user, post) pair, a new row is inserted; if a prior row exists with deleted_at set, the reaction is re-activated by clearing deleted_at.

Security and authorization follow the actors domain: the reacting principal must be an authenticated user from civic_board_users. Application logic must enforce reaction policy from civic_board_reaction_policies, including that reactions are globally enabled (enabled=true), allowed on posts (allow_on_posts=true), and disallow self-like when allow_self_like=false. If max_reactions_per_user_per_day is present, rate limiting must be applied using civic_board_rate_limits as needed. The target post is validated using civic_board_posts.status to ensure reacting to Published content; Hidden or Deleted posts must reject new reactions for non-admin actors per requirements.

This operation relates to multiple Prisma entities. It writes to civic_board_post_reactions and reads civic_board_posts to validate status and ownership (for self-like prevention). It may also read civic_board_reaction_policies to check feature flags and quotas. The unique constraint on civic_board_post_reactions (civic_board_user_id, civic_board_post_id) guarantees a single active reaction per pair and supports idempotent behavior: calling create when an active reaction already exists simply returns the current record. Session linkage and audit can be recorded via civic_board_user_sessions and civic_board_audit_logs for traceability.

Validation and business rules include: the postId must reference an existing civic_board_posts.id; the actor must not be suspended (civic_board_users.suspended=false); reacting to one’s own post must be rejected when policies prohibit self-like; reacting to Hidden/Deleted posts must be rejected for non-admin users; daily per-user reaction quotas, if configured, must be enforced. Related operations include DELETE /posts/{postId}/reactions to deactivate the reaction for the same user/post pair.

Error handling expectations: not found or unavailable outcomes when the post is not visible; policy-disabled outcomes when reactions are turned off; ownership/policy violations for self-like attempts; quota/rate-limit outcomes when daily caps are exceeded; and idempotency where creating an already-active reaction returns the existing active state without duplication.

The underlying Prisma model civic_board_reaction_policies defines these columns: id (UUID, primary key), code (unique human-readable policy identifier), enabled (global feature toggle), allow_on_posts, allow_on_comments, allow_self_like, optional max_reactions_per_user_per_day (Int, nullable), plus created_at/updated_at timestamps and a deleted_at timestamp used to mark logically removed rows for retention/purge cycles. No denormalized counters are stored in this table, and configuration values are intended to be read by application logic at runtime.
operations.description:
List and search reaction policy configurations to determine runtime behavior of the reactions feature. The civic_board_reaction_policies schema comment states it is an “Administrative policy controlling whether reactions are enabled and under what constraints,” including whether reactions are allowed on posts and/or comments and whether self-like is permitted. Each row carries a unique code, boolean feature flags, an optional per-user daily cap, and lifecycle timestamps.

Security and access: This is a read-only configuration query. While administrative UIs manage these records, clients may read them to shape UX (for example, disabling like buttons when enabled is false). Sensitive values are not stored here; therefore, this endpoint may be public in read-only form, with additional server-side checks safeguarding any write operations elsewhere.

Database relationship and behavior: This operation reads directly from civic_board_reaction_policies. The model defines a unique code (code) for business-friendly selection and exposes boolean flags: enabled, allow_on_posts, allow_on_comments, allow_self_like, and optional max_reactions_per_user_per_day for guardrails. Timestamps created_at and updated_at support auditability. The deleted_at timestamp is used to mark records as logically removed; searches should exclude rows with a non-null deletion timestamp to present only active policies.

Validation and query rules: The request body supports pagination (page, pageSize), sorting (e.g., by created_at or code), and filtering by flags and code equality/substring where appropriate. Because code is globally unique by @@unique([code]), client code may also rely on GET by code to fetch a single record. If filters conflict or produce no matches, an empty page is returned with zero total.

Related operations: Use GET /reactionPolicies/{reactionPolicyCode} to fetch a single configuration by its unique code. Administrative creation or modification endpoints are out of scope for this read-only operation and would require appropriate authorization if introduced.

Error handling: Invalid pagination inputs or unsupported sort fields are normalized to safe defaults. Requests are rate limited via separate systemic controls; when limits are exceeded, the system returns a standard rate-limited outcome. Records marked as logically removed are not returned.

Only administrators may execute this action. Provider logic should also emit an audit entry into civic_board_audit_logs describing the action (e.g., action: "reaction_policy.delete", target_table: "civic_board_reaction_policies", target_id: <policy id>), but audit logging is internal to the service and not exposed via this API.

The selection relies on civic_board_reaction_policies.code (global scope uniqueness via @@unique([code])). If the code does not exist or the row is already marked deleted (deleted_at IS NOT NULL), the service should respond with a not-available outcome to avoid leaking internal state. Because policy rows influence runtime behavior of reactions on posts and comments, removing a policy should be coordinated with configuration reads; clients are responsible for selecting an appropriate fallback policy after deletion.

Validation notes: reactionPolicyCode must be a non-empty string and match an existing, currently active policy (deleted_at IS NULL). Business logic should prevent deletion when the policy is the only active policy required by the platform’s configuration. Related operations typically include creating or updating reaction policies; reads should filter out rows with deleted_at set.

Error handling expectations: not found/not available for unknown codes; conflict if a guard prevents deletion (e.g., active/default policy); and generic failure handling consistent with service-wide exception rules. operations.specification: Provide an administrator dashboard overview aggregating moderation-related metrics across multiple tables. This read-only operation composes data from: civic_board_reports (queue of user-submitted reports and statuses), civic_board_moderation_actions (admin resolutions with decision values such as "No Action", "Hide", "Delete"), civic_board_posts (status: "Published" | "Hidden" | "Deleted"), and civic_board_comments (status: "Published" | "Hidden" | "Deleted"). It returns a computed DTO (ICivicBoardModerationOverview) summarizing pending counts, recent decision trends, and visibility distributions. No single Prisma table maps to the response; results are computed via SQL aggregations (e.g., COUNTs grouped by status/decision, date-bucketed trends).
operations.description:
This operation returns a consolidated moderation overview for administrators. It summarizes the current state of user-reported items from civic_board_reports ("User-submitted moderation requests ... status such as 'pending' or 'resolved'") alongside resolution records stored in civic_board_moderation_actions ("Captures the acting admin and session with the chosen decision 'No Action' | 'Hide' | 'Delete'"). Additionally, it includes visibility distributions of content from civic_board_posts (status with "Published", "Hidden", "Deleted" and timestamps such as published_at/edited_at) and civic_board_comments (status with the same values) to help admins understand the moderation footprint.

Security and permissions: Access is restricted to admins because the response may include sensitive moderation pipeline information and counts of hidden or deleted content. Provider logic should record an administrative read audit in civic_board_audit_logs for visibility into dashboard access while keeping the endpoint itself read-only.

Underlying entities and relationships: reports can be specialized to posts via civic_board_report_of_posts and to comments via civic_board_report_of_comments; each report can have at most one civic_board_moderation_action resolution. Aggregations typically include: number of pending reports, resolved reports by decision, recent (e.g., last 7 or 30 days) resolution counts, counts of posts and comments by status, and optionally per-day buckets derived from created_at or published_at for trend lines.

Validation and behavior: This endpoint does not accept filters in the minimal scope and always returns the current overview snapshot. If needed later, a PATCH variant could add time window or scope parameters. It never modifies any data. Related operations include report queue listing and resolution endpoints. Error handling should follow general rules: unauthorized for non-admin actors and system-busy/temporary errors where applicable.

operations.specification: Compute aggregated moderation statistics grouped by reason across all report records. This operation reads from the civic_board_reports table (primary source for report metadata) and produces a summary of total counts per reason. The specialization tables civic_board_report_of_posts and civic_board_report_of_comments are not directly grouped but guarantee target binding and duplicate prevention at creation time via their composite uniqueness constraints; counting is performed at the main civic_board_reports layer to avoid double-counting. Records with deleted_at set are excluded from aggregation to reflect active historical data. Example SQL (conceptual): SELECT reason, COUNT(*) AS count FROM civic_board_reports WHERE deleted_at IS NULL GROUP BY reason ORDER BY count DESC.

operations.description:
Return a system-wide summary of moderation reports grouped by their categorical reason. The underlying data comes from the civic_board_reports model, which stores the reporter-selected reason, optional note, workflow status, and timestamps (created_at/updated_at). By summarizing at the main report layer, the service provides an at-a-glance view of where moderation attention is focused without exposing individual report details.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to administrators because it reveals platform-wide moderation patterns. The reports table is described as user-submitted moderation requests with a workflow state such as "pending" or "resolved." This endpoint respects logical removals by excluding rows where deleted_at is present so that the summary reflects currently retained report data per policy.

From a data relationship perspective, each civic_board_reports row must be bound to exactly one specialization row in either civic_board_report_of_posts or civic_board_report_of_comments. Those specialization models record reporter identity, target (post or comment), and session, and also enforce duplicate prevention via composite uniqueness (same user cannot report the same item twice). This aggregation intentionally groups only by civic_board_reports.reason and does not attempt to re-join to targets, ensuring consistent counting semantics.

Validation and behavior: the reasons are treated as free-form categorical values per schema comments (validated at the application layer during report creation). This endpoint groups whatever categorical values exist in the data. If no reports exist, the result contains an empty collection. Related administrative endpoints may include queues or detailed report listings, but those are distinct from this high-level summary.

responseBody.description: Aggregated counts by report reason for moderation analytics.

The operation groups by the UTC calendar day derived from created_at and counts how many reports were filed on each day. Specialization tables civic_board_report_of_posts and civic_board_report_of_comments are not required for aggregation but ensure that each report has a concrete target and that duplicates are prevented at creation time. Records with deleted_at set are excluded to align with retention behavior. Conceptual SQL: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at) AS day, COUNT(*) AS count FROM civic_board_reports WHERE deleted_at IS NULL GROUP BY day ORDER BY day DESC.

The data is sourced from the civic_board_reports model, which records each report’s reason, optional note, workflow status, and timestamps. Grouping is performed on created_at truncated to day in UTC, yielding the number of reports submitted each calendar day.

This endpoint is intended for administrative use only because it exposes system-wide moderation activity levels. Consistent with the schema’s lifecycle fields, rows where deleted_at is populated are excluded to reflect active retained data. The summary does not expose individual reporter identities or target references, honoring the principle of presenting aggregated information only.

Entity relationships: while every report is specialized via exactly one of civic_board_report_of_posts or civic_board_report_of_comments, this aggregation operates at the main civic_board_reports layer and does not join to the specializations. This avoids double-counting and keeps the computation efficient. Expected behavior: if no reports exist for a given day range, the time series will omit those days (sparse series). Clients may post-process to backfill missing dates if a continuous series is desired. Related operations include reason-based summaries and administrative queues that surface pending vs resolved counts.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves aggregated analytics for content reports by querying the Moderation domain tables centered on civic_board_reports and its specializations civic_board_report_of_posts and civic_board_report_of_comments. It supports time-window filtering (created_at), categorical slicing by reason and status, and breakdowns by target type (post vs comment). The provider composes SQL that groups and counts report records, optionally joining to Articles tables (civic_board_posts, civic_board_comments) to respect current visibility/status fields when required by filters. The endpoint is designed for administrative dashboards to monitor reporting trends and moderation workload. It does not create or modify any data; it summarizes existing rows.

The primary Prisma DB tables referenced are:
- civic_board_reports: carries reason, note, status, created_at/updated_at columns and is the anchor for analytics.
- civic_board_report_of_posts and civic_board_report_of_comments: identify the concrete target and reporter context and enforce duplicate-prevention via composite unique constraints.
- Optionally, civic_board_moderation_actions: used to slice metrics by resolved outcomes when joining on civic_board_report_id.

The request body accepts search/filter parameters modeled as ICivicBoardReport.IRequest (e.g., time range based on created_at, reason/status filters, and target-type selector). The response returns a computed analytics object ICivicBoardReportAnalytics containing counts and breakdowns suitable for dashboards (totals, by-reason, by-status, and time-bucket series).
operations.description:
Retrieve administrative analytics summarizing user-submitted content reports. The computation is anchored on the civic_board_reports table, whose columns include reason (categorical reason such as Spam/Harassment/Off-topic/Other), optional note, status (queue state like "pending" or "resolved"), and created_at/updated_at timestamps. The specialization tables civic_board_report_of_posts and civic_board_report_of_comments bind each report to its concrete target and reporter identity. Their composite uniqueness constraints (user+post or user+comment) allow detection of duplicates for analytics purposes without over-counting.

This endpoint is restricted to administrative actors because it exposes system-level operational insights. Use it to monitor volume over time, top reasons, resolution funnel, and distribution across posts versus comments. Implementations may optionally join to civic_board_moderation_actions to attribute decisions (e.g., "Hide", "Delete", "No Action") and to Articles tables (civic_board_posts, civic_board_comments) when filtering by current content status is necessary for policy reviews. The analytics query respects the provided filters and time windows and returns only aggregate structures; it never returns personal emails or raw free-text notes.

From a data-model perspective, analytics derive from:
- civic_board_reports: core event rows with reason, status, created_at.
- civic_board_report_of_posts / civic_board_report_of_comments: target-type discrimination, reporter and session context, and uniqueness guarantees to avoid double-counting.
- civic_board_moderation_actions: one-to-one resolution records per report, enabling breakdowns by decision.

Validation rules follow the underlying schema: reason and status filters must align with values stored in civic_board_reports; date filters apply to created_at ranges; and target-type accepts only post or comment determined by the specialization linkage. When no data matches, the endpoint returns zeroed totals with empty arrays. Authorization failures return an access-denied outcome, and malformed filters result in validation errors describing which field is incorrect.
operations.summary: Administrative analytics for reports based on civic_board_reports and related specialization tables.

email.description: Login and contact email for the member. Maps to civic_board_users.email (unique).

display_name.description: Public display name shown on authored content. Maps to civic_board_users.display_name.

ip.description: Optional client IP address captured for session context. Used to create civic_board_user_sessions.ip during self-signup. Accepts IPv4 or IPv6 when provided; null permitted. When omitted, the server may derive it from the request origin.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) captured for session context. Used to create civic_board_user_sessions.href during self-signup.

referrer.description: Referrer URL captured for session context. Used to create civic_board_user_sessions.referrer during self-signup. May be an empty string when the user arrives directly (no referrer).

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are included to create an initial civic_board_user_sessions record at join time. Column references: civic_board_users.email, civic_board_users.password_hash (derived from password), civic_board_users.display_name; session columns civic_board_user_sessions.ip/href/referrer are populated by the server.

id.description: Unique identifier of the user (UUID). Maps to civic_board_users.id.

display_name.description: Public display name shown on authored content. Maps to civic_board_users.display_name.

email_verified.description: Whether the member’s email has been verified. Non-nullable in Prisma and safe to expose for context. Maps to civic_board_users.email_verified.

suspended.description: Whether the account is currently suspended (restricted from creating/modifying content). Non-nullable in Prisma and safe to expose for context. Maps to civic_board_users.suspended.

ICivicBoardUser.ISummary.description: User summary derived from Prisma model civic_board_users. Optimized for embedding and admin-safe reads. It includes identification (id), display name, status indicators (email_verified, suspended), and created_at for sorting/administration while explicitly excluding sensitive fields such as email and password_hash.

current_password.description: Current credential submitted by the authenticated user to verify ownership prior to changing the password. Server compares this plain text against the stored hash in civic_board_users.password_hash. This field is never persisted; only the verification result is used.

new_password.description: New credential to be set for the account. The server hashes this secret and stores the result in civic_board_users.password_hash, updating civic_board_users.updated_at upon success. Business logic may enforce strength/complexity rules; clients must send the plain text value (never a hash).

ICivicBoardUserPassword.IUpdate.description: Request DTO for in-session password change for the currently authenticated member (authorizationActor: "user"). No actor identifiers (e.g., user_id, session_id) are accepted from the client—identity is derived from the JWT/session. On success, the backend updates civic_board_users.password_hash and revokes other sessions by setting civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at, leaving the current session active.

ok.description: Indicates whether the password change completed successfully, including updating civic_board_users.password_hash and applying session revocations for other sessions.

revoked_sessions.description: Number of other sessions that were terminated by setting civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at for records linked via civic_board_user_sessions.civic_board_user_id, excluding the current session.

message.description: Concise human-readable outcome message (e.g., "Password updated; 3 other sessions were signed out"). Useful for UX display. Optional and for client guidance only.

ICivicBoardUserPassword.ISummary.description: Response DTO summarizing the result of an in-session password change. Reflects whether the update to civic_board_users.password_hash succeeded and how many other user sessions were revoked (expired). Contains no sensitive data or tokens.

id.description: Primary key of the user session (UUID).

user.description: Owner member transformed from civic_board_user_sessions.civic_board_user_id as a summary reference. Replaces the raw FK and aligns with the BELONGS-TO d�3e .ISummary rule.

ICivicBoardUserSession.ISummary.description: Summary of a user session used for audit context. Includes the owning user as a summary object and connection metadata with timestamps. The raw foreign key civic_board_user_id is not exposed; instead, the BELONGS-TO relation is transformed into user: ICivicBoardUser.ISummary for complete context and consistency with admin session summaries.

email.description: Administrator login and contact email. Will populate civic_board_admins.email (unique).

password.description: Plain-text password for registration; the backend hashes it and stores into civic_board_admins.password_hash. Clients must NEVER send pre-hashed values.

display_name.description: Public-facing administrator display name (civic_board_admins.display_name). Shown in audit trails and moderation records.

ip.description: Client IP address observed at session establishment. Optional because servers can derive it; recorded in civic_board_admin_sessions.ip when provided.

href.description: Connection URL at the moment of registration; used for session context and audit. Recorded in civic_board_admin_sessions.href.

referrer.description: Referrer URL captured at session creation; may be an empty string for direct access. Recorded in civic_board_admin_sessions.referrer.

ICivicBoardAdminJoin.ICreate.description: Admin self-registration (join) request body. On success, a new row is created in civic_board_admins (email, password_hash via secure hashing of provided password, display_name, email_verified=false, suspended=false, timestamps) and an authenticated session is recorded in civic_board_admin_sessions (civic_board_admin_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at). This DTO intentionally excludes system-managed fields and uses plain password per security guidance. Session context fields follow the Session Table Pattern: href and referrer are required for self-join; ip is optional and may be derived server-side.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated administrator. Maps to civic_board_admins.id (UUID).

admin.description: Profile summary of the authenticated administrator. Derived from civic_board_admins with sensitive credentials excluded (no password_hash).

ICivicBoardAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Authorized administrator response object returned by authentication flows (join, login, refresh). It carries the admin actor's unique id from civic_board_admins.id and a structured token bundle for subsequent authenticated requests. The admin property provides a concise profile based on civic_board_admins while excluding sensitive fields such as password_hash.

This DTO is not a direct table mapping. It aggregates data from civic_board_admins and ephemeral authorization services (JWT issuance) and is used as the canonical response body for admin authentication operations.

id.description: Unique identifier of the admin. Maps to civic_board_admins.id.

display_name.description: Administrator display name shown in audit trails and moderation records. Maps to civic_board_admins.display_name.

email_verified.description: Indicates whether the admin’s email was verified. Maps to civic_board_admins.email_verified.

suspended.description: Whether the admin account is suspended from taking privileged actions. Maps to civic_board_admins.suspended.

created_at.description: Administrator account creation timestamp (UTC). Maps to civic_board_admins.created_at. Useful for audit context and sorting.

ICivicBoardAdmin.ISummary.description: Lightweight administrator reference used in other entities’ summaries. Fields map to civic_board_admins. Excludes authentication secrets and internal tokens by design. Includes created_at for audit/sorting parity with user summaries.

email.description: Administrator email credential. Must match civic_board_admins.email (unique).

password.description: Administrator password in plain text for verification against civic_board_admins.password_hash. Never stored; the backend hashes and compares securely.

ip.description: Client IP address for session context. Optional; server may extract from request (IPv4 or IPv6). Included here for SSR or proxied scenarios.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) where login was initiated. Required to populate civic_board_admin_sessions.href (VarChar(80000)).

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) captured at login. Required to populate civic_board_admin_sessions.referrer (VarChar(80000)). May be an empty string when direct access occurs.

ICivicBoardAdminLogin.ICreate.description: Administrator login request DTO. Validates credentials against civic_board_admins (email, password_hash) and establishes a session row in civic_board_admin_sessions capturing connection context (ip, href, referrer). Per security guidance, href and referrer are required; ip is optional and may be provided or captured server-side. This type does not map directly to a single Prisma model as it drives multiple actions (auth verification and session creation).

refresh_token.description: Opaque refresh token presented by the administrator to obtain new access/refresh credentials. Although no corresponding column exists in the Prisma schema, this value is verified server‑side against the active session and token subsystem associated with civic_board_admin_sessions for audit context. Do not include session context fields (ip, href, referrer) here; refresh reuses the established session per security rules.

ICivicBoardAdminRefresh.ICreate.description: Request DTO to refresh administrator authorization without re‑entering credentials. This operation does not write to any Prisma model directly; it validates the provided refresh token and, on success, issues new authorization material. Audit and analytics may reference civic_board_admin_sessions (id, civic_board_admin_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at) but those identifiers are never supplied by clients in this body.

delivery.description: Optional delivery hints for issuing the admin email verification message. Identity and recipient email are derived from the authenticated admin; this object only guides presentation and routing.

ICivicBoardEmailVerification.ICreate.description: Request DTO to issue an email verification token for the currently authenticated admin. Server creates a row in civic_board_email_verifications (actor_type = "admin", email, token, expires_at, used = false) and links it via civic_board_email_verification_of_admins (civic_board_email_verification_id, civic_board_admin_id). No actor identifiers or email should be supplied by the client—these are derived from the authenticated admin (JWT) and the admin’s record in civic_board_admins. This DTO now optionally carries delivery hints (channel/locale/href/referrer) for parity with the user variant; rate limiting may be enforced via civic_board_rate_limits and audit entries may be written to civic_board_audit_logs.

oneOf.description: Actor discriminator value used across polymorphic ownership patterns. In civic_board_email_verifications and civic_board_password_reset_tokens, the actor_type column identifies a regular user target.

Actor discriminator value used across polymorphic ownership patterns. In civic_board_email_verifications and civic_board_password_reset_tokens, the actor_type column identifies an administrator target.

IECivicBoardActorType.description: Actor discriminator values used across polymorphic ownership patterns (e.g., email verifications and password reset tokens). Allowed values are "user" and "admin"; these appear in civic_board_email_verifications.actor_type and civic_board_password_reset_tokens.actor_type.

id.description: Primary Key. Maps to civic_board_email_verifications.id (UUID).

actor_type.description: Discriminator indicating which actor type this verification targets ("user" | "admin"). Mirrors civic_board_email_verifications.actor_type.

email.description: Email address captured at token issuance. Mirrors civic_board_email_verifications.email; used for audit and delivery traceability.

expires_at.description: Token expiration timestamp in UTC. Mirrors civic_board_email_verifications.expires_at. Tokens are invalid after this time.

used.description: Whether the verification token has been consumed. Mirrors civic_board_email_verifications.used.

used_at.description: Timestamp when the token was consumed, if applicable. Mirrors civic_board_email_verifications.used_at (UTC).

created_at.description: Creation timestamp (UTC) when the verification token row was inserted. Mirrors civic_board_email_verifications.created_at.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp (UTC) for the verification token record. Mirrors civic_board_email_verifications.updated_at.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp (UTC) for retention or legal hold workflows. Mirrors civic_board_email_verifications.deleted_at; null when active.

ICivicBoardEmailVerification.ISummary.description: Summary view of an email verification token as stored in civic_board_email_verifications. Excludes sensitive fields (e.g., the secret token value) while exposing lifecycle attributes required for administrative or audit contexts. Adds optional lifecycle columns (used_at, updated_at, deleted_at) to accurately reflect the entity state without compromising security.

token.description: Opaque verification token string issued by civic_board_email_verifications.token. The backend consumes this to confirm email ownership for actor_type="admin" in this operation.

ICivicBoardEmailVerificationConfirm.ICre.description: Request payload to confirm an administrator's email by consuming a previously issued token from civic_board_email_verifications. Security note: Only the token is accepted from the client; actor identity and permissions are resolved server-side using the token linkage. Implementations SHOULD treat this flow as idempotent (reusing an already-consumed token yields a consistent outcome) and MAY apply rate limiting for invalid attempts using civic_board_rate_limits.

success.description: Indicates whether the requested security operation completed successfully. This covers flows such as email verification, password reset, password change, logout, and session revocation described for civicBoard administrators.

operation.description: Logical name of the operation that produced this outcome. Constrained to IEAdminSecurityOperation for predictable client handling.

admin_id.description: Identifier of the affected administrator (civic_board_admins.id). Returned for correlation and client-side routing. Never includes sensitive fields like password_hash.

email_verified.description: When present, reflects the administrator’s current email verification status after processing. For example, set to true on successful verification using civic_board_email_verifications and civic_board_email_verification_of_admins.

password_rotated.description: When present, indicates a password rotation occurred (e.g., via password reset or password change). The underlying prisma model column updated is civic_board_admins.password_hash; the clear-text password is never exposed in responses.

sessions_revoked.description: When present, the number of administrator sessions that were ended by setting expired_at on civic_board_admin_sessions as part of the operation (e.g., password reset or explicit session revocation).

session_expired.description: When true, indicates the caller’s current session was terminated (logout flow).

message.description: Human-friendly summary of the outcome suitable for UI display. Does not expose internal details or secrets.

occurred_at.description: UTC timestamp when the operation was finalized on the server. Provided for audit-friendly client UX. The authoritative audit trail is recorded in civic_board_audit_logs.

ICivicBoardAdmin.ISecurityOutcome.description: Generic security outcome for administrator-focused flows. Aggregates side effects recorded in Prisma models such as civic_board_admins (email_verified, password_hash), civic_board_admin_sessions (expired_at), and the audit table civic_board_audit_logs. The operation field is constrained by IEAdminSecurityOperation to ensure consistency across integrations; occurred_at is required for predictable timelines. No password material or tokens are ever returned in this type.

current_password.description: Current administrator credential in plain text for verification (must be non-empty). The backend validates this against civic_board_admins.password_hash and never stores or logs the plain value. Do NOT supply any admin identifiers here; the authenticated admin is derived from the session/JWT.

new_password.description: New administrator credential in plain text (min 8, max 2000 characters, aligned with admin join policy). The backend will hash this value and update civic_board_admins.password_hash. Historical sessions in civic_board_admin_sessions for this admin may be expired as part of rotation per security policy.

ICivicBoardAdminPassword.IUpdate.description: Password change request for the currently authenticated administrator. This DTO carries only business inputs (plain current and new passwords with explicit length constraints). It intentionally does not expose database columns or actor IDs. Internally, the service verifies current_password against civic_board_admins.password_hash and, on success, replaces it with a new hash and expires prior civic_board_admin_sessions (except possibly the current session per policy).

reason.description: Optional human-readable reason for logging out (e.g., "user_initiated", "security_rotation"). Used for audit trails in civic_board_audit_logs; not persisted on civic_board_admins or civic_board_admin_sessions beyond standard expired_at update.

ICivicBoardAdminLogout.ICreate.description: Logout request for the currently authenticated administrator. Invoking this operation will mark the active row in civic_board_admin_sessions as expired (sets expired_at) using the caller’s session context. No admin identifiers are accepted from the client—the actor is determined from authentication.

mode.description: Revocation scope selector. Determines whether all sessions for the authenticated administrator are revoked, or all sessions except the current session are revoked.

ICivicBoardAdminSessionsRevoke.ICreate.description:
Request body for revoking administrator sessions recorded in civic_board_admin_sessions. This DTO MUST NOT accept any administrator identifiers — the authenticated admin and current session are derived from the JWT/session context. The backend updates rows in civic_board_admin_sessions by setting expired_at according to the selected mode.

Prisma reference:
- civic_board_admin_sessions: id, civic_board_admin_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at (nullable).
- civic_board_admins: unchanged by this operation (email, password_hash, display_name, email_verified, suspended).

page.description: 1-based page index for pagination of civic_board_configurations list results.

limit.description: Maximum number of items per page to return for civic_board_configurations listing.

search.description: Free-text search applied to key and description fields. Implementations may leverage the GIN trigram index defined on description per Prisma schema comments.

key.description: Optional exact or prefix filter on the unique configuration key (civic_board_configurations.key).

include_deleted.description: Whether to include soft-deleted rows (deleted_at is not null). Defaults to false to return only active records.

effective_since_from.description: Inclusive lower bound filter for effective_since (UTC).

effective_since_to.description: Inclusive upper bound filter for effective_since (UTC).

created_at_from.description: Inclusive lower bound filter for created_at (UTC).

created_at_to.description: Inclusive upper bound filter for created_at (UTC).

updated_at_from.description: Inclusive lower bound filter for updated_at (UTC).

updated_at_to.description: Inclusive upper bound filter for updated_at (UTC).

order_by.description: Field to sort by. Only whitelisted sortable columns are allowed.

order_direction.description: Sort direction for the chosen order_by field.

ICivicBoardConfiguration.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for listing platform configurations from civic_board_configurations. This DTO represents request criteria only and does not directly map to a Prisma model.

Prisma reference (civic_board_configurations):
- Business key: key (unique)
- Optional typed value columns: value_string, value_int, value_double, value_boolean, value_uri
- Metadata: description, effective_since, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at (soft delete)
- Indexes: created_at, effective_since, and GIN trigram on description for efficient search.

IESortDirection.description: Alias of the canonical IESortOrder ("asc" | "desc"). Prefer using IESortOrder; this type is retained for backward compatibility to avoid duplication and drift.

ICivicBoardConfiguration.description: System configuration entity mapped to Prisma model civic_board_configurations. Each record is an independent key-value configuration used to toggle features, define numeric thresholds, ratios, booleans, or URIs across the platform. Only one of the typed value columns is expected to be populated for a given row (value_string, value_int, value_double, value_boolean, or value_uri). This DTO exposes the complete configuration including metadata and audit timestamps as documented in the Prisma schema comments.

id.description: Primary key of the configuration row. Maps to civic_board_configurations.id (UUID).

key.description: Unique business identifier for this configuration (e.g., "public_read", "attachments.max_count"). Maps to civic_board_configurations.key and is globally unique.

value_string.description: String-typed configuration value when applicable. Maps to civic_board_configurations.value_string. Only one typed value field is expected to be used per row.

value_int.description: Integer-typed configuration value when applicable (e.g., numeric limits). Maps to civic_board_configurations.value_int. Only one typed value field is expected to be used per row.

value_double.description: Decimal-typed configuration value when applicable (e.g., thresholds or ratios). Maps to civic_board_configurations.value_double. Only one typed value field is expected to be used per row.

value_boolean.description: Boolean-typed configuration value when applicable (e.g., feature toggle). Maps to civic_board_configurations.value_boolean. Only one typed value field is expected to be used per row.

value_uri.description: URI-typed configuration value when applicable (e.g., callback URL, CDN endpoint). Maps to civic_board_configurations.value_uri. Only one typed value field is expected to be used per row.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the configuration purpose and usage. Maps to civic_board_configurations.description.

effective_since.description: Optional timestamp indicating when this configuration became effective. Maps to civic_board_configurations.effective_since (UTC).

created_at.description: Creation timestamp in UTC. Maps to civic_board_configurations.created_at.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp in UTC. Maps to civic_board_configurations.updated_at.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp for retention and operational safety. Maps to civic_board_configurations.deleted_at (UTC).

ICivicBoardConfiguration.ICreate.description: Create DTO for system configurations mapped to Prisma model civic_board_configurations. Requires a globally unique key and allows at most one typed value field to be provided among value_string, value_int, value_double, value_boolean, and value_uri. Optional metadata includes description and effective_since. System-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are excluded from requests.

key.description: Unique business identifier code of the configuration (e.g., "public_read", "attachments.max_count"). Maps to civic_board_configurations.key and must be globally unique.

value_string.description: String-typed configuration value required for this variant. Maps to civic_board_configurations.value_string. Exactly one typed value field may be set per create request.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the configuration purpose and usage. Maps to civic_board_configurations.description.

effective_since.description: Optional timestamp indicating when the configuration becomes effective (UTC). Maps to civic_board_configurations.effective_since.

ICivicBoardConfiguration.ICreate.IWithSt.description: Create variant requiring `key` and `value_string`, forbidding all other typed value fields. This maps to Prisma model civic_board_configurations and allows optional metadata (`description`, `effective_since`). Exactly one typed value field is allowed per create request; this variant uses the string value.

ICivicBoardConfiguration.ICreate.IWithIn.description: Create variant requiring value_int and forbidding other typed value fields. Includes the unique configuration key and optional metadata. Only one typed value field may be provided in a single request.

key.description: Unique business identifier code of the configuration (e.g., "public_read", "attachments.max_count"). Maps to civic_board_configurations.key and must be globally unique.

value_int.description: Integer-typed configuration value to set for this configuration. Exactly one typed value field is allowed per create request; this variant uses value_int. Maps to civic_board_configurations.value_int.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the configuration purpose and usage. Maps to civic_board_configurations.description.

effective_since.description: Optional timestamp indicating when the configuration becomes effective (UTC). Maps to civic_board_configurations.effective_since.

ICivicBoardConfiguration.ICreate.IWithDo.description: Create variant requiring value_double and forbidding other typed value fields. Includes the unique configuration key and optional metadata. Only one typed value field may be provided in a single request.

key.description: Unique business identifier code of the configuration (e.g., "public_read", "attachments.max_count"). Maps to civic_board_configurations.key and must be globally unique.

value_double.description: Double-precision configuration value to set for this configuration. Exactly one typed value field is allowed per create request; this variant uses value_double. Maps to civic_board_configurations.value_double.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the configuration purpose and usage. Maps to civic_board_configurations.description.

effective_since.description: Optional timestamp indicating when the configuration becomes effective (UTC). Maps to civic_board_configurations.effective_since.

ICivicBoardConfiguration.ICreate.IWithBo.description: Create variant requiring value_boolean (non-null) and forbidding other typed value fields. Exactly one typed value column may be provided per request (boolean in this variant). Includes the unique key and optional metadata. Maps to Prisma model civic_board_configurations.

key.description: Unique business identifier code of the configuration (e.g., "public_read", "attachments.max_count"). Maps to civic_board_configurations.key (unique).

value_boolean.description: Boolean-typed configuration value to persist in civic_board_configurations.value_boolean. Exactly one typed value field is allowed per row; other typed value fields must not be provided in this variant.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the configuration purpose and usage. Maps to civic_board_configurations.description (nullable).

effective_since.description: Optional timestamp indicating when the configuration becomes effective (UTC). Maps to civic_board_configurations.effective_since (nullable).

ICivicBoardConfiguration.ICreate.IWithUr.description: Create variant requiring value_uri (non-null) and forbidding other typed value fields. Exactly one typed value column may be provided per request (URI in this variant). Includes the unique key and optional metadata. Maps to Prisma model civic_board_configurations.

key.description: Unique business identifier code of the configuration (e.g., "public_read", "attachments.max_count"). Maps to civic_board_configurations.key (unique).

value_uri.description: URI-typed configuration value to persist in civic_board_configurations.value_uri (VarChar(80000)). Exactly one typed value field is allowed per row; other typed value fields must not be provided in this variant.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the configuration purpose and usage. Maps to civic_board_configurations.description (nullable).

effective_since.description: Optional timestamp indicating when the configuration becomes effective (UTC). Maps to civic_board_configurations.effective_since (nullable).

ICivicBoardConfiguration.ICreate.IWithou.description: Create variant that provides no typed value fields; creates a placeholder configuration with only key and optional metadata. This variant explicitly forbids providing any typed value column to avoid overlapping with other create variants.

key.description: Unique business identifier code of the configuration (e.g., "public_read", "attachments.max_count"). Maps to civic_board_configurations.key and must be globally unique.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the configuration purpose and usage. Maps to civic_board_configurations.description.

effective_since.description: Optional timestamp indicating when the configuration becomes effective (UTC). Maps to civic_board_configurations.effective_since.

ICivicBoardConfiguration.IUpdate.description: Update DTO for civic_board_configurations keyed by `key` in the path parameter. Modifies metadata (description, effective_since) and at most one typed value column among value_string, value_int, value_double, value_boolean, or value_uri. System-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are excluded. The `key` MUST NOT appear in the body to avoid duplicating the path parameter. Only a single typed value column is expected to be used per row; this DTO enforces "at most one provided" via oneOf constraints.

ICivicBoardPolicy.IRequest.description: Search and pagination DTO for listing civic_board_policies with administrative filters, sorting, and pagination. This is a request container (not directly mapped to a Prisma model). Supports filters on policy_code, name, category, enabled, effective window intersection (starts_at/ends_at), and created/updated time ranges. Default behavior excludes soft-deleted rows unless include_deleted is true. Prisma columns referenced: policy_code, name, category, enabled, value_string, value_int, value_double, starts_at, ends_at, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.

page.description: 1-based page index for pagination. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Page size (items per page). Defaults to 20; capped to 100 to protect performance.

order_by.description: Field to sort by. Policies support ordering by created_at or updated_at.

name_contains.description: Substring match filter for civic_board_policies.name. Backed by trigram index for efficiency.

category_equals.description: Filter by exact category value. Provide null to find rows where category IS NULL.

effective_window.description: Intersection filter against the policy’s effective window (starts_at/ends_at). Records intersecting this range should match.

created_between.description: Filter records whose created_at falls within the given inclusive range.

updated_between.description: Filter records whose updated_at falls within the given inclusive range.

include_deleted.description: When true, include rows with non-null deleted_at; otherwise exclude soft-deleted rows.

IDateTimeRange.description: Inclusive date-time range used for filtering windows. Provide either `from`, `to`, or both. Timestamps use ISO 8601 in UTC. When both are provided, the range is inclusive on both ends (from <= value <= to).

oneOf.description: Sortable fields for civic_board_policies administrative listings. Values correspond to Prisma columns created_at and updated_at.
Sortable fields for civic_board_policies administrative listings. Values correspond to Prisma columns created_at and updated_at.

IECivicBoardPolicyOrderBy.description: Sortable fields for civic_board_policies administrative listings. Values correspond to Prisma columns created_at and updated_at.

id.description: Primary key of the policy row. Prisma model civic_board_policies.id (UUID).

policy_code.description: Stable, globally unique business identifier of the policy (e.g., "public_read", "attachments.policy", "report.duplicate_cooldown_hours"). Maps to civic_board_policies.policy_code and is unique by @@unique([policy_code]).

name.description: Human-friendly policy name for administrative UIs. Maps to civic_board_policies.name.

category.description: Optional category for grouping related policies (e.g., "visibility", "attachments", "reporting"). Maps to civic_board_policies.category; nullable.

enabled.description: Whether the policy is currently enabled. For value-carrying policies, this indicates if enforcement is active. Maps to civic_board_policies.enabled.

value_string.description: Optional string value carried by the policy. Only one of the typed value columns is typically used per row. Maps to civic_board_policies.value_string; nullable.

value_int.description: Optional integer value carried by the policy. Only one of the typed value columns is typically used per row. Maps to civic_board_policies.value_int; nullable.

value_double.description: Optional double precision value carried by the policy. Only one of the typed value columns is typically used per row. Maps to civic_board_policies.value_double; nullable.

starts_at.description: Optional start of the policy’s effective window (UTC). Maps to civic_board_policies.starts_at; nullable.

ends_at.description: Optional end of the policy’s effective window (UTC). Maps to civic_board_policies.ends_at; nullable.

notes.description: Administrative notes describing policy rationale or change context (not shown to end users). Maps to civic_board_policies.notes; nullable.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp (UTC). Maps to civic_board_policies.created_at.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp (UTC). Maps to civic_board_policies.updated_at.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp for retention and operational safety. Maps to civic_board_policies.deleted_at; nullable.

ICivicBoardPolicy.description: Policy entity representing a single configuration/policy record per Prisma civic_board_policies. This table stores platform policies such as public-read, moderation defaults, and feature switches. Each row carries a stable policy_code (unique), human-friendly name, enabled flag, optional category, optional typed value (exactly one of string/int/double is typically used), optional effective window (starts_at/ends_at), optional notes, and audit timestamps.

ICivicBoardPolicy.ICreate.description: Create payload for civic_board_policies. Requires a globally unique policy_code, a human-friendly name, and enabled flag. Optional fields include category, one typed value column (value_string OR value_int OR value_double), an effective window (starts_at/ends_at), and administrative notes. System-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are excluded.

ICivicBoardPolicy.IUpdate.description: Update DTO for civic_board_policies identified by {policyCode} in the path. Supports partial updates to: name, category, enabled, a single typed value column (value_string OR value_int OR value_double), starts_at, ends_at, notes. Do NOT include id or policy_code in the body. When both starts_at and ends_at are provided, providers should verify coherent windows (starts_at <= ends_at).

page.description: Page index for pagination (1-based). Default determined by server policy.

limit.description: Page size limit. Default and maximum are enforced by server policy (suggested max 200).

actor_type.description: Filter by actor type captured in civic_board_audit_logs.actor_type. Allowed values mirror the canonical audit actor enum.

actor_id.description: Filter by actor identifier (UUID), when applicable. Maps to civic_board_audit_logs.actor_id.

actor_session_id.description: Filter by actor session identifier (UUID). Maps to civic_board_audit_logs.actor_session_id.

action.description: Filter by business action name (e.g., "post.create", "policy.update"). Uses trigram search when the server supports it.

outcome.description: Filter by outcome summary (e.g., "success", "failure:rate_limited"). May use exact or trigram partial matching depending on server implementation.

target_table.description: Filter by target table name (e.g., "civic_board_posts"). Maps to civic_board_audit_logs.target_table.

target_id.description: Filter by target resource identifier (UUID). Maps to civic_board_audit_logs.target_id.

ip.description: Filter by IP address (exact or prefix). Server may accept IPv4/IPv6 values.

created_from.description: Inclusive start of created_at range filter (UTC).

created_to.description: Inclusive end of created_at range filter (UTC).

q.description: Keyword search across action/outcome/message using trigram indexes for efficient fuzzy matching.

oneOf.description: Sort by audit log creation time (UTC). Default when omitted.
Sort by audit log update time (UTC).

order_dir.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc for newest-first listings.

include_deleted.description: When true, include soft-deleted audit log rows (where deleted_at IS NOT NULL). Default is false to exclude soft-deleted entries.

ICivicBoardAuditLog.IRequest.description: Search and filtering DTO for listing civic_board_audit_logs. Read-only query parameters used by admin-only endpoint. Supports pagination, sorting (created_at/updated_at), keyword search (q), and filters on actor, target, IP, and created_at range. Business rule: Access restricted to administrators; server typically excludes rows where deleted_at is not null.

ICivicBoardAuditLog.description: Audit trail entity mapped to Prisma table civic_board_audit_logs. This record captures who did what and when, with optional request/session context for security investigations. Properties are derived from the Prisma schema comments: actor_type, optional actor_id and actor_session_id (stored as UUID text without FK coupling), action, outcome, optional target_table and target_id hints, connection metadata (ip, href, referrer), an optional human-readable message, and timestamps (created_at, updated_at). Soft-deletion (deleted_at) supports retention/legal hold workflows.

id.description: Primary key (UUID). Unique identifier of the audit event row.

actor_type.description: Type of actor initiating the event (e.g., "user", "admin", "system"). Stored as raw text to avoid cross-domain foreign keys; constrained here by the canonical enum.

actor_id.description: Identifier of the actor (UUID) when applicable. Nullable and not FK-bound to avoid domain coupling.

actor_session_id.description: Identifier of the actor session (UUID) when applicable. Nullable and not FK-bound.

target_table.description: Target table name when the action is scoped to a specific resource (e.g., "civic_board_posts").

target_id.description: Target resource identifier when applicable (UUID), stored without FK.

ip.description: Observed IP address for the request context, when available. Stored as text; may contain IPv4 or IPv6.

href.description: Full request URL when available (connection URL). Large varchar in Prisma for traceability.

message.description: Optional human-readable message or error context to aid investigations.

created_at.description: Event creation timestamp (UTC).

updated_at.description: Administrative update timestamp (UTC). Usually equals created_at for immutable entries.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp (UTC) for retention or legal hold workflows. Null when active.

ICivicBoardRateLimit.IRequest.description: Search criteria, pagination, and sorting options for administrative inspection of rate-limit windows in Prisma table civic_board_rate_limits. This request DTO is not a direct table mapping. It supports filtering by scope(s), actor_type(s), optional actor_id (UUID), time windows over window_started_at/window_ends_at, inclusion of soft-deleted rows, and saturated-only condition (count >= limit). It also allows page/limit pagination and controlled sorting.

limit.description: Page size (items per page). Capped to protect service performance.

scopes.description: Filter by one or more logical action scopes (e.g., "post.create", "comment.create", "report.create", "login.failed").

actor_types.description: Filter by actor types. Allowed values are constrained by IECivicBoardRateLimitActorType: "user", "admin", "ip".

actor_id.description: Filter by a specific actor identifier (UUID). Null can be used to explicitly search for records with NULL actor_id when supported by the backend.

include_deleted.description: When true, include records where deleted_at is not null. Default is false to exclude administratively retired rows.

saturated_only.description: When true, return only windows where count >= limit (saturated). Evaluated at query time.

oneOf.description: Sort key applied to the result set. Must be one of the enumerated fields supported by the backend.
