generated_at.description: Timestamp (UTC) when this overview snapshot was computed. Computed at read time, not persisted. Useful alongside civic_board_audit_logs when auditing dashboard accesses.

reports.description: Aggregations derived from civic_board_reports (main report metadata) with specialization integrity from civic_board_report_of_posts / civic_board_report_of_comments.

moderation_actions.description: Recent administrative resolution trends derived from civic_board_moderation_actions, grouped into per-day buckets and decision counts.

content_visibility.description: Distribution of content visibility for posts and comments based on civic_board_posts.status and civic_board_comments.status.

ICivicBoardModerationActionOverview.description: Consolidated moderation dashboard overview for administrators. This DTO is computed by aggregating across multiple Prisma models: civic_board_reports (user-submitted reports and statuses), civic_board_moderation_actions (admin resolutions), civic_board_posts (status/time fields), and civic_board_comments (status/time fields). No single table maps to this type; it is produced by SQL aggregations and business logic at read time. Includes pending counts, resolved-by-decision breakdowns, recent decision trends, and visibility distributions.

pending_count.description: Number of reports currently pending review (e.g., civic_board_reports.status = 'pending' per application logic). Excludes soft-deleted rows (deleted_at IS NULL filter expected).

resolved_count.description: Number of reports that have been resolved (e.g., linked civic_board_moderation_actions present, or civic_board_reports.status = 'resolved').

total_count.description: Total number of currently retained reports (pending + resolved) from civic_board_reports where deleted_at IS NULL.

resolved_by_decision.description: Breakdown of resolved reports by the moderation decision captured in civic_board_moderation_actions.decision (e.g., 'No Action', 'Hide', 'Delete').

ICivicBoardModerationActionOverview.IRep.description: Aggregated snapshot of the reports pipeline based on civic_board_reports and civic_board_moderation_actions. Designed for admin overview cards and charts.

decision.description: Resolution outcome grouped from civic_board_moderation_actions.decision. Values are constrained by IEModerationDecision (e.g., "No Action", "Hide", "Delete").

count.description: Non-negative count of moderation actions for the given decision within the aggregation bucket (may be 0).

ICivicBoardModerationActionOverview.IDec.description: Count of moderation actions grouped by a single decision value. The decision maps directly to civic_board_moderation_actions.decision (constrained by IEModerationDecision), and count is a non‑negative integer representing how many actions with that decision occurred in the bucket (0 permitted).

last_7_days.description: Exactly 7 UTC calendar-day buckets for the last 7 days (inclusive), ordered by date ascending. This series is anchored to ICivicBoardModerationOverview.generated_at (UTC). Providers MUST include a bucket for every day in the window, even when there were zero moderation actions that day.

last_30_days.description: Exactly 30 UTC calendar-day buckets for the last 30 days (inclusive), ordered by date ascending. This series is anchored to ICivicBoardModerationOverview.generated_at (UTC). Providers MUST include a bucket for every day in the window, even when there were zero moderation actions that day.

ICivicBoardModerationActionOverview.IMod.description: Recent moderation activity trends grouped by calendar day and anchored to the overview snapshot’s generated_at (UTC) timestamp. Each series contains a fixed number of UTC calendar‑day buckets (7 and 30 respectively), ordered ascending by date, and MUST include zero‑activity days to satisfy the fixed bucket counts. For each day’s bucket (ICivicBoardModerationOverview.IDecisionTrendBucket), providers SHOULD include one ICivicBoardModerationOverview.IDecisionCount per value of IEModerationDecision (e.g., "No Action", "Hide", "Delete"), allowing zero counts for decisions that did not occur, to promote a consistent array shape across buckets.

date.description: UTC calendar date for this bucket (YYYY-MM-DD) typically derived from civic_board_moderation_actions.created_at.

ICivicBoardModerationActionOverview.IDec.description: Per-day aggregation bucket of moderation actions with decision breakdowns.

posts_by_status.description: Counts of civic_board_posts grouped by status (Published | Hidden | Deleted).

comments_by_status.description: Counts of civic_board_comments grouped by status (Published | Hidden | Deleted).

ICivicBoardModerationActionOverview.ICon.description: Visibility distribution for posts and comments based on their status fields.

status.description: Business visibility state from civic_board_posts.status or civic_board_comments.status.

count.description: Number of records in this status.

ICivicBoardModerationActionOverview.IVis.description: Count of records for a specific content visibility status.

ICivicBoardEmailVerificationOfUser.IConf.description:
Confirmation outcome for user email verification. Returned by POST /auth/user/email/verify/confirm after consuming a valid token from civic_board_email_verifications via civic_board_email_verification_of_users.

Contract notes:
- When verified = true, verified_at is required and provides the UTC timestamp of confirmation.
- When verified = false, verified_at MAY be omitted or null; a descriptive message SHOULD be provided to indicate an outcome such as invalid/expired/already-used token or already verified account.

This DTO contains no token material or sensitive identifiers and is independent of direct Prisma row mapping.

ICivicBoardEmailVerificationOfUser.IIssu.description:
Acknowledgement payload for email verification token issuance returned by POST /auth/user/email/verify/request.

Security: Does NOT include the secret token. Prisma linkage on success: civic_board_email_verifications (actor_type = "user") specialized via civic_board_email_verification_of_users.

Contract notes:
- When issued = true, expires_at is REQUIRED and indicates the token expiry time.
- When issued = false, providers MAY set already_verified = true to indicate no issuance.

Usage Note: This schema is intended for the issuance endpoint only.

oneOf.description:
Enumeration of supported administrator security operations used in ICivicBoardAdmin.ISecurityOutcome.operation for contract consistency across flows.

Values:
- admin.email_verification.verify: Admin email verification confirmation using a token from civic_board_email_verifications linked via civic_board_email_verification_of_admins.
- admin.password_reset.request: Admin password reset token issuance request (writes to civic_board_password_reset_tokens and specialization).
- admin.password_reset.reset: Admin password reset confirmation using a valid reset token; rotates password_hash and may revoke sessions.
- admin.password.change: Authenticated admin password change (verifies current credential, rotates password_hash, revokes prior sessions).
- admin.logout: Explicit termination of the current admin session by setting expired_at on civic_board_admin_sessions.
- admin.sessions.revoke: Bulk revocation of admin sessions (all or all except current) by setting expired_at on civic_board_admin_sessions.

IECivicBoardAuditLogActorType.description: Actor discriminator for audit logs. Allowed values mirror business usage across the platform: "user", "admin", "system". Maps to civic_board_audit_logs.actor_type.

scenario.draft: Confirming a password reset with an invalid token should fail without changing any credentials. Steps: (1) Call password reset confirm with a clearly invalid/random token string and a nominal new password. (2) Expect a 4xx outcome indicating token not found/invalid/expired and ensure no password change occurs for any account. Edge case: use multiple malformed tokens to ensure consistent handling.

An authenticated member changes their password by providing the correct current password. Steps: (1) Register a new member via join and obtain the access token. (2) Call update password with current password and a new strong password; expect a success summary and that other sessions are revoked per policy while the current session remains valid. (3) Try changing the password again using the old (now invalid) current password to confirm it fails. Business validations: ownership via auth context, suspended=false enforcement, password_hash rotated, and session revocation behavior for other sessions (no extra sessions created in this test).

dependencies.purpose: Establish an authenticated user context (new member) to authorize the password update operation.

scenario.draft: Validate that password reset requests for non-existent admin emails return the same generic acknowledgement to prevent account enumeration. Steps: (1) Choose a unique, unissued admin email value. (2) Call POST /auth/admin/password/reset/request with that email. (3) Assert a success acknowledgement is returned (no error), with no token or sensitive details leaked. (4) Optionally repeat the request to confirm consistent uniform responses across attempts.

Ensure a non-owner cannot delete another user’s post via the user-scoped delete endpoint. Join as User A and create a post. Join as User B (separate user context) and attempt DELETE /civicBoard/user/posts/{postId} for User A’s post. Expect permission denied (e.g., 403) and no state change to the post. Confirms ownership enforcement: only the author (or an admin via the admin route) can delete the post.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as User A (post author) to create the target post
Create a post under User A to be targeted by the non-owner deletion attempt
Authenticate as User B (non-owner) to attempt unauthorized deletion

scenario.draft: Verify that deleting an already soft-deleted configuration produces a not-available outcome. Workflow: 1) Create an admin context via join. 2) Create a configuration with a unique key to target. 3) Delete it once successfully. 4) Attempt a second DELETE for the same key and confirm the service reports not-available (already removed). 5) Validate that repeated deletes are not treated as successful idempotent operations for already-removed records per specification wording.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin for privileged operations.
Create a configuration record to target for deletion attempts.

scenario.draft:
Validate that a freshly joined member can successfully refresh access using a valid refresh artifact tied to an active session, and then use the renewed access token on a protected user endpoint that does not require email verification.

Workflow:
1) Create a brand-new member context via POST /auth/user/join to obtain an initial authorized payload (access and refresh artifacts) and establish an active civic_board_user_sessions row (expired_at is null).
2) Call POST /auth/user/refresh with the refresh artifact. Expect 200 with a new authorized payload. Do not assert on refresh rotation; assert that the response is authorized and usable.
3) Use the newly returned access token to call POST /auth/user/logout/others. Expect success to confirm the refreshed token is accepted by a protected user route (no email verification required).
4) Business validations: session must remain active prior to step 3; refresh should succeed because the session was not revoked.

dependencies.purpose: Establish a new authenticated member session and obtain the refresh artifact required by the refresh operation.

scenario.draft:
Ensure that refresh fails when the underlying session has been terminated, enforcing civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at semantics.

Workflow:
1) Create a new member via POST /auth/user/join to obtain access and refresh artifacts tied to an active session.
2) Immediately end the current session using POST /auth/user/logout (sets civic_board_user_sessions.expired_at).
3) Attempt POST /auth/user/refresh with the previously obtained refresh artifact. Expect an authorization failure (e.g., 401/403) because the session is no longer active.
4) Business validations: the server must not issue new tokens for expired sessions; error messaging should not leak sensitive details.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a new member and obtain the refresh artifact bound to the newly created session.
Terminate the current session by setting expired_at so that subsequent refresh attempts are invalid.

scenario.draft:
Ensure the email verification request endpoint rejects unauthenticated calls, enforcing that only a signed-in user can request a verification token for their own account.

Workflow:
1) Invoke POST /auth/user/email/verify/request without any Authorization header.
2) Expect an authorization failure (e.g., 401/403). Validate that no token is issued and no user context is inferred.
3) Business validation: the endpoint must not allow anonymous requests to issue tokens or infer email ownership.

Security workflow: requesting a password reset with an unknown email must return the same acknowledgement as with an existing email, preventing account enumeration.

Steps:
1) Call POST /auth/user/password/reset/request using an email that does not exist in the system.
2) Optionally compare status code and response envelope to the existing-email scenario to ensure they are indistinguishable.

Validations:
- Response status and body shape match the existing-email case (uniform acknowledgement).
- No error details should disclose whether the email exists.

Validate that an attachment’s metadata can be publicly retrieved when its parent post is Published. Workflow: (1) Create a fresh user context via join. (2) As that user, create a post (status=Published by business rules). (3) As the same user, upload/register a valid attachment under the post. (4) Without authentication (public), call GET /civicBoard/posts/{postId}/attachments/{attachmentId} and expect success with immutable metadata returned (uri, original_filename, content_type, byte_size, optional image dimensions). (5) Ensure records with deleted_at are not returned and that returned data matches the created attachment. This validates composition, visibility inheritance from a Published post, and public accessibility of attachment metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a user to create the post and attachment required for public retrieval.
Create a Published post to host the attachment.
Upload/register an attachment under the created post to obtain attachmentId for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Business workflow: Validate search, filtering, and sorting capabilities for attachments under a published post. Steps: (1) Member joins. (2) Member creates a post. (3) Member uploads multiple attachments with diverse content_type and byte_size values. (4) Publicly call PATCH /civicBoard/posts/{postId}/attachments with various filters (e.g., filename substring, content_type in [image/jpeg, application/pdf], byte_size ranges) and sort orders. (5) Validate that returned items match criteria, pagination is stable, and ordering aligns with parameters. Confirm no authentication is needed for Published parent posts. Note: Use join-only for member setup; do not use login.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a member to prepare the parent post and attachments.
Create a published post to scope the attachment listing.
Upload multiple attachments to enable meaningful filtering and sorting tests.

scenario.draft: Verify that attachments cannot be updated when the parent post has been soft-deleted. Workflow: (1) Join as a user and create a post. (2) Upload an attachment under that post. (3) Soft-delete the parent post (status set to "Deleted" with deleted_at). (4) Attempt PUT /civicBoard/user/posts/{postId}/attachments/{attachmentId} as the original author. (5) Expect a denial because the parent post is deleted. (6) Confirm attachment remains unchanged after the failed update attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as member (user) to create and manage content.
Create the parent post to host the attachment.
Upload an attachment under the created post.
Soft-delete the parent post to validate blocked behavior on attachment update.

scenario.draft:
Business goal: Verify that when the parent post is soft-deleted, the public reaction-count endpoint for a surviving comment under that post becomes unavailable due to parent visibility rules.

Workflow:
1) Create an author via join and create a Published post.
2) Create a comment under that post as the author.
3) Soft-delete the parent post via DELETE /civicBoard/user/posts/{postId}.
4) Call GET /civicBoard/comments/{commentId}/reactions/count without authentication and expect a not-available outcome because the comment inherits visibility from the parent post’s state.

Validations:
- Confirm that the comment existed and was Published prior to parent deletion.
- After post deletion, public access to the comment’s reaction count should be denied.
- No login is used; only join is used for setup authentication.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the author to create post and comment and then delete the parent post.
Create the Published post that will later be soft-deleted.
Create a Published comment under the post (provides commentId).
Soft-delete the parent post to verify the comment count endpoint becomes unavailable.
